metadata.description: Twelve plugins for coding sessions: solo-skills (every skill that stands alone, in one install), code-desk (quality contract, focus, board triage, and status comms), diagrams (structural diagrams), atelier (tiered delegation agents and session-discipline hooks), kaneo (work tracked on a live Kaneo board), mise-en-place (an in-repo _meta planning system for board-less repos), obsidian-toolkit (Obsidian plugin development), pocketbase (build and operate PocketBase backends), carbon (IBM Carbon Design System via the hosted Carbon MCP server), bun (the bun toolchain as the default JS and TS runtime), kenn-forge (maintainer triage over a running kenn-forge daemon), and plugin-feedback (report a plugin defect without leaving the session).

plugins.description: Delegate work to model-tiered agents instead of doing it all in one session: size the task, pick a delegation architecture, and dispatch scoped slices to scouts, builders, reviewers, and managers. Skills cover orchestration, session handoff, backlog waves, and a review cycle that runs before work lands. Hooks watch the context watermark, keep the handoff fresh and surface it on cold start, isolate writing workers in their own git worktrees, hold protected config in custody, and refuse a worker git call that would sweep away a sibling's uncommitted work or land on a protected branch. Enforcement follows the main checkout into a linked worktree, so an isolated worker is no longer an unguarded one. Run /atelier:activate to arm it in a project and see what each hook resolved. Release history: https://github.com/hsb3/dotfiles-agents/releases.
plugins.name: atelier

plugins.description: Bun as the default JS/TS runtime, package manager, test runner, and bundler — command mapping from npm/node habits, built-ins that replace dependencies, measured traps (bunfig exclusions, PATH order, mise interop), and a worked npm→bun migration. Release history: https://github.com/hsb3/dotfiles-agents/releases.
plugins.name: bun

plugins.description: Build and audit IBM Carbon Design System UIs with IBM's own tooling packaged as one install: the official carbon-builder skill (vendored verbatim at a pinned upstream ref) driving the hosted Carbon MCP server this plugin registers — component/variant/prop search, docs and accessibility guidance, Carbon Charts source, Carbon Labs, and code-compliance audits — plus the official docs-index fallback and IBM's prompt-writing guidance for when the server is unreachable. The hosted server requires an IBM-approved account (authenticate via /mcp). Release history: https://github.com/hsb3/dotfiles-agents/releases.
plugins.name: carbon

plugins.description: Set a project's starting conditions and run the work through them: interview the owner into a written quality contract, build and red-prove the one gate command that enforces it, then keep the release loop honest — mid-session focus and scope checks, weekly board triage through a backend adapter (GitHub Projects, Kaneo, Kata), recurring status comms rendered as themed PowerPoint decks, READMEs backed by live screenshots, and the project-memory taxonomy. The in-repo _meta planning system that used to ship here now lives in the mise-en-place plugin. Release history: https://github.com/hsb3/dotfiles-agents/releases.
plugins.name: code-desk

plugins.description: Structural diagrams for repo docs, decks, and briefings, with consistent SVG and PNG output: Mermaid for GitHub-rendered markdown, Python diagrams for cloud architecture with provider icons, draw.io reading and headless export, Excalidraw sketches, and raw Graphviz. Data charts belong to the dataviz skill, deck theming to pptx-themes. Release history: https://github.com/hsb3/dotfiles-agents/releases.
plugins.name: diagrams

plugins.description: Track a repo's work on a live Kaneo board instead of in-repo task files, so parallel sessions stop claiming the same task and no branch grows its own backlog. Ships the workflow skill, the task-authoring skill (write tracker items a cold agent can execute), the board's MCP server definition, a reference manager agent, and hooks that keep claim authority in the root session, block board writes while the config is incomplete, catch a stray MCP registration that would silently authenticate the owner instead of the agent, stamp every write with its agent and session, and deny subagent Bash that reaches the board host directly. Configure with five KANEO_* env vars; nothing about an instance is baked in. Release history: https://github.com/hsb3/dotfiles-agents/releases.
plugins.name: kaneo

plugins.description: Maintainer-workflow triage over a running kenn-forge daemon — PR/issue review, diffs and CI checks, local review state, and coding-agent handoff. Two surfaces over the same daemon API: the kenn_forge_* MCP tools for an agent driving its own loop, and the kenn-forge CLI for shell, scripts, and humans. The daemon must be running locally; the MCP surface additionally needs it enabled in the daemon config. Release history: https://github.com/hsb3/dotfiles-agents/releases.
plugins.name: kenn-forge

plugins.description: An in-repo _meta/ planning system: a documented directory standard, a read-only compliance audit against it, an additive-only scaffolder that fills exactly the gaps the audit found, and a planning desk under _meta/plans/ holding one build plan per unit of work. The standard, the audit, and the scaffold assume the repo tree is the system of record, so install them only where that is true. The desk is the exception: it reads work items from a tracker through a pluggable adapter, and a Kata adapter ships. Release history: https://github.com/hsb3/dotfiles-agents/releases.
plugins.name: mise-en-place

plugins.description: Build Obsidian plugins against the real API — lifecycle, settings, vault operations, commands, chat and copilot sidebar UIs, in-plugin MCP servers over Streamable HTTP — and automate vaults from the terminal with the official Obsidian CLI. Release history: https://github.com/hsb3/dotfiles-agents/releases.
plugins.name: obsidian-toolkit

plugins.description: File a bug or feature request against a plugin you are using without leaving the session. Hooks tell the primary session and its dispatched workers what each may file, and a stdlib reporter writes the issue to a fixed template instead of a free-handed gh call. Release history: https://github.com/hsb3/dotfiles-agents/releases.
plugins.name: plugin-feedback

plugins.description: Build and operate PocketBase backends: an operational skill for driving a running instance (collection and record CRUD, auth, backups, migration generation, Go hooks and custom routes), a design skill of 63 prioritized rules for schema, API rules, auth flows, query performance, realtime, files, and deployment, and three subject-matter agents that carry the backend laws into a delegated brief: a builder, an adversarial reviewer, and a security auditor, each proving its claims from its own clean-room server. Release history: https://github.com/hsb3/dotfiles-agents/releases.
plugins.name: pocketbase

plugins.description: Every skill that stands on its own, in one install instead of a shelf of one-skill plugins: harness and environment config, session discipline, research, diagrams and data visualization, repo and project setup, comms, sandboxed opencode instances, and Obsidian plugin development. Membership is derived, not curated — a gate re-reads the skill bodies every run and keeps out anything that needs a companion agent or hook, plus a documented exemption class for skills that prescribe an opt-in system the consumer chooses deliberately, in-repo or external. Release history: https://github.com/hsb3/dotfiles-agents/releases.
plugins.name: solo-skills
